messages:
incident-bot: Pager: SRV lookup error rate >5% for consul.service.discovery in us-west-3 (az3). Severity: P2. Affected: internal service discovery, increased 5xx on inference routing. Link: https://incidents.internal/3300012345 :rotating_light:
eng_oncall_maria: acked. I'm on call, will triage now.
eng_oncall_maria: quick check - is this isolated to az3 or cross-az?
netops_jon: netflow shows packet drops between az3 and consul leader in az1. BGP sessions fine but we're seeing TCP retransmits to consul port 8500 from az3.
platform_carol: seeing elevated SRV NXDOMAIN and SERVFAIL for queries proxied through coredns in az3. Upstream consul requests timing out ~250-500ms.
sre_dave: any recent deploys to consul or coredns in az3?
platform_carol: no consul deploys in last 24h. coredns had a config roll 6h ago but only changed logging.
eng_oncall_maria: good to know. Maria attaching runbook excerpt: consul-srv-resolution > network-flap. Steps: 1) verify consul members, 2) check leader, 3) failover traffic to az1/az2, 4) scale coredns replicas.
eng_oncall_maria: running: `kubectl -n infra get pods -l app=consul -o wide`
eng_oncall_maria: output: `consul-0 (az1) Ready`, `consul-1 (az2) Ready`, `consul-2 (az3) NotReady - CrashLoopBackOff`
netops_jon: that matches TCP issues. consul-2 healthcheck failing to reach raft peers.
eng_oncall_maria: `consul members` shows consul-2 in failed state, raft snapshot warnings in logs. Sharing tail: ```consul: log: failed to replicate raft log: timeout contacting peer 10.2.3.4```
product_ash: customers may see routing errors to hosted endpoints served from az3. Any estimate of customer impact?
eng_oncall_maria: initial metrics: ~2.8% client 5xx increase across hosted API (mostly requests hitting specific SRV-backed services), spike started ~T-12m. Not global but noticeable for some tenants pinned to az3.
sre_dave: mitigation plan: 1) remove consul-2 from gossip/raft to allow cluster to stabilize, 2) drain coredns in az3, 3) reroute traffic for model-serving to az1/az2 via smart-routing policy, 4) if necessary, scale up consul-servers in az1.
netops_jon: I'll prepare a network workaround: announce a static route to force consul-2 traffic to a healthy egress path in az3 (temporary). Will push in 2-3m.
platform_carol: scaling coredns now: `kubectl -n infra scale deployment coredns --replicas=6` (was 3).
eng_oncall_maria: removing consul-2 from peers now: `consul leave -address=10.2.3.5` executed (via ssh to consul-2).
eng_oncall_maria: consul cluster showing quorum restored (2/3) and leader stable in az1.
platform_carol: draining coredns pods in az3: `kubectl cordon node-az3-dns-1` then `kubectl delete pod coredns-xxx` - new pods landing in az1/az2.
netops_jon: route announcement applied for az3 consul egress - monitoring for packet loss.
eng_oncall_maria: smart-routing rule applied to shift ~70% of new SRV lookups to az1/az2 for the affected service; TTL reduction in place for faster convergence.
product_ash: can we confirm which customers routed through az3 are affected so CS can notify?
sre_dave: querying usage map, sending list in DM to CS. Roughly 3 mid-market customers and a handful of dev accounts, none on Dedicated.
eng_oncall_maria: system checks: SRV error rate down to 0.9% after the reroute, client 5xx back to baseline within 6m.
platform_carol: consul-2 logs show disk pressure + raft timeouts; we should reprovision swap/disk later.
netops_jon: network workaround holding; retransmits down from 28% to 2%.
eng_oncall_maria: marking incident as mitigated for now. Will keep thread open for root cause & follow-up.
product_ash: thanks, Maria. Please provide a 1-paragraph customer impact statement for CS/ops.
eng_oncall_maria: "Between 12:18–12:30 UTC, we observed elevated SRV lookup failures from services in us-west-3 (az3) due to a Consul server node experiencing raft replication timeouts caused by transient egress packet loss. This led to a small increase (~2.8%) in client 5xx for customers with traffic pinned to az3. We rerouted SRV lookups to healthy AZs, drained DNS pods in az3, and removed the failed Consul node from the cluster; error rates returned to baseline within ~12 minutes. No persistent data loss; dedicated customers unaffected. Follow-up actions: reprovision disk on consul-2, add richer egress path monitoring, and add an automated raft-removal runbook step."
sre_dave: assigning follow-ups: ticket INF-4721 (reprovision consul-2 disk), INF-4722 (egress path alert), INF-4723 (runbook update).
eng_oncall_maria: handing to daytime oncall @netops_jon for network follow-up and to @platform_carol for platform remediation. I'll update status page and close pager. :white_check_mark:
netops_jon: taking network follow-up, will post progress in INF-4722.
platform_carol: taking platform follow-up, will schedule consul node reprovisioning during low traffic window.
incident-bot: Incident 3300012345 status changed: mitigated -> monitoring.
